source_location: ISO 32000-2:2020 §7.9.3, printed p.117 / physical p.132; read with §7.9.2.2.1. The operative sentence qualifies a stream by its unencoded bytes and says they follow text-string encoding, byte-order, and lead-byte requirements.
effective_errata: No direct annotation on §7.9.3 physical p.132 changes this rule. EC3 #214 (global terminology note on physical p.10; visible strikes on Table 32 physical pp.124–125) removes the nonexistent qualifier 'name' before 'string'; for /Renditions, the effective encoding is specifically UTF-16BE. It does not amend the byte interpretation required by §7.9.3.
ledger: §7.9.3 is implemented. Prior inventory row 7.9.3.text_stream_uses_decoded_text_string_bytes correctly forwards the property-specific consumers rather than asserting one universal decode site.
assertions: crates/pdf-model/tests/text_strings_spec_audit.rs::a_filtered_utf8_text_stream_uses_the_text_string_encoding_after_decoding (exact-xref compressed stream through field appearance; BOM and café expected; no-recovery, decoded-byte, visible-output, empty and equivalent-string controls)
crates/pdf-model/tests/script_unread.rs (Table 221 /JS stream path is exercised for size accounting, but only plain ASCII script bytes)
crates/viewer-core/tests/open_sequence.rs (Table 32 /JavaScript name-tree opening path is exercised with a string-valued /JS; runner is intentionally absent)
crates/pdf-model/tests/forms_data.rs (FDF script structures and text-string handling; not a Table 32 consumer)
assessment: Field /V, popup /RC, and script code call filter decoding before text_string, matching the source's unencoded-byte requirement. Existing assertions provide independent visible output and a positive script-stream route, but no public assertion combines Table 32 /JavaScript name-tree dispatch with filtered Unicode text-stream decoding. Drafted a bounded assertion for that combination.
verdict: implementation-supported; targeted public script-text-stream assertion gap
residuals: The prior field stream test is not proof that every property consumer dispatches text streams correctly. Not a finding that ASCII script streams fail or that the common text decoder is wrong. FDF §12.7.8.3.1 uses similar types but is a separate consumer.

source_location: ISO 32000-2:2020 §7.9.5, printed p.118 / physical p.133. Required representation: array of four numbers giving diagonally opposite corners. The lower-left/upper-right order is described as typical, not mandatory. The note explicitly permits zero width or height.
effective_errata: Primary physical p.133 has no clause-changing annotation. The PDF's annotations there concern §7.9.4 date text and links, not the rectangle paragraph; no §7.9.5 erratum was identified.
ledger: §7.9.5 is implemented; existing feature inventory decomposes arity/type, corner order, zero extent, and writer output.
assessment: Current implementation normalizes each diagonal axis; a public annotation raster test demonstrates the swapped-corner case. A zero-extent rectangle is retained as a rectangle while the distinct MediaBox requirement for a physical medium causes substitution. The writer assertion checks exactly four numeric members and deliberately does not require the typical ordering.
verdict: sampled requirements and assertions align; no new gap found
residuals: At-least-four tolerant parsing and ignoring extras are recovery behavior for malformed input, not a proven violation of this producer-facing representation rule. No claim that every rectangle-bearing consumer was audited here.

source_location: ISO 32000-2:2020 §7.7.4, Table 32 printed p.108–109 / physical pp.123–124. Name dictionary is reached via Catalog /Names; each of its keys is a root name tree. Effective rows are Dests, AP, JavaScript, Pages, Templates, IDS, URLS, EmbeddedFiles, AlternatePresentations, Renditions.
effective_errata: EC3 #214 globally changes 'name string' to 'string'; its Table 32 strike overlays are on physical pp.124–125. #214 additionally changes Renditions' key encoding requirement to UTF-16BE. EC3 #672 places 'deprecated in PDF 2.0' on IDS and URLS by carets on physical p.124. These locations were checked in the primary annotated PDF; processed Markdown alone omits the overlays.
ledger: §7.7.4 is marked implemented, but prior clause-progress had no review artifacts. Ownership is distributed: Dests → §12.3.2.4; AP → §12.5.5; JavaScript → §12.6.4.17; Pages/Templates → §12.7.7; EmbeddedFiles → §7.11.4/§14.13; IDS/URLS → deprecated Web Capture; AlternatePresentations/Renditions → §13 media. Other assigned shards review those behavior owners.
assertions: crates/viewer-core/tests/open_sequence.rs (document-level library name tree; currently string /JS and no-runner behavior)
media_viability shard for Renditions/AlternatePresentations; not recertified here
assessment: Key-specific ownership is represented in code/tests; Table 32 does not require a reader to resolve appearance streams by their name. §12.5.5 expressly says AP names have no standard meanings and no PDF object may refer to an appearance stream by name. The current named_appearances tests correctly read the tree generically and bind a widget's appearance via object reference. IDS/URLS are deprecated in PDF 2.0, not silently treated as currently active features. Existing tests exercise a Table 32 script name tree but only with string script payloads.
verdict: sampled key consumer paths supported; script stream encoding gap separately drafted
residuals: No exhaustive certification of each key's downstream feature, encrypted-wrapper filename rule, deprecated Web Capture, or media playback. Those are independently owned. The AP test's general tree walk does not imply arbitrary name-based appearance lookup is required.
